Tamban V3: engineering audit and revised implementation

Verdict: the existing system is a working part-model baseline, not yet a validated individual-fish grader. The new implementation separates these targets rather than disguising body or part detections as whole fish. No original image, label, notebook, or checkpoint is overwritten.

1. Evidence available and verification boundary

Inputs inspected directly: the cleaned Tamban_v9_Cleaned_Training_Pool.zip, its active box labels and original polygon backups, the latest Tamban_YOLO26_COMPLETE_CELL.ipynb, its actual source code, and the earlier dataset/cleanup reports. The cleaned ZIP SHA-256 is 4061dcd9d940b86f0c957acbe024766d3b5812eb15776b8b19d96b19274ca4a2.

The user supplied successful Colab training logs through epoch 40. However, the trained last.pt, feature-model binary and full runtime result archive are not attached to this conversation. A path printed by Colab is not a locally accessible checkpoint. There is also no independent, reviewed whole-fish validation/test dataset. Consequently, no actual learned-model precision, recall, mAP, grading F1, confusion matrix, count error, or performance improvement is reported here.

The authoring environment has CPU PyTorch but no CUDA GPU and no installed Ultralytics. Attempts to reach package downloads from the runtime were unavailable. Thus YOLO training, real-checkpoint prediction, GPU timing and live Colab interaction remain untested. The delivered tests exercise data, geometry, evaluation and feature code instead. The workbench can inspect the user's actual Drive checkpoint in Colab, read-only.

Body appearances are NOT unique biological fish. The box-overlap measurements are proxies for crowding, not proof of physical occlusion. The continuous-coordinate boundary count differs from the more conservative rasterized crop count (2,433); the descriptive shape screen used rasterized crops. Neither count establishes an actually missing head or tail.

The cleaned pool passed the mechanical checks, but targeted visual inspection is not expert verification of every retained label. Absence of malformed boxes does not prove correct grades or exhaustive object coverage.

Class balance

Grade Bodies Heads Tails Part total
A 275 230 226 731
B 470 477 288 1,235
C 3,042 2,343 1,379 6,764
Rejected 1,208 1,126 556 2,890

C has about 11.1 times A's body appearances and 6.5 times B's. This supports class-aware experimental sampling and better A/B specimen diversity, not blindly deleting C or erasing visible labels. The new trainer retains ordinary sampling as the baseline and exposes class-image sampling as an optional controlled experiment. The feature branch weights capture groups and grades, but weighting cannot create independent specimens.

Scene composition and dependence

The retained scene labels are A-only 97, B-only 80, C-only 434, Rejected-only 190, and A+Rejected 45. Thus 801/846 (94.7%) are single-grade scenes, with no retained B+C mixed scenes.

Timestamped B images come from August 23, 20:34:04-20:47:10; timestamped C images from August 23, 21:45:01-22:10:56. Their scene conditions remain coupled to grade. A conservative dark-background measurement, excluding expanded annotation boxes and white padding, has median grayscale means 9.65 for B and 16.21 for C. This is descriptive association, not a new background-classifier accuracy result or a physical lighting measurement.

The four near-scene pairs were visually inspected and have highly similar arrangements. All now belong to TRAINING. They are not current train-test leakage, because the cleanup retired the old evaluation splits. They still demonstrate pseudo-replication risk: a future random split could separate familiar fish into opposing partitions. File hashes cannot authenticate physical identities.

Annotation masks are not equivalent to fish silhouettes

Active labels are detection boxes. Original polygon backups are part-level outlines, not whole-fish instances. Closed rectangles often contain five vertices because the first point is repeated; counting only four-vertex rows would misclassify them.

Correctly accounting for closure, 4,411/11,620 original part polygons are rectangles. Rectangle rates differ markedly by grade: B 84.3%, C 22.4%. Among body annotations alone, the rates are B 81.7% and C 15.2%. This difference can contaminate naive comparisons using annotation geometry or foreground selected inside those boxes. Detailed polygons should not be assumed to provide comparable masks across classes.

3. Main code problems and implemented responses

Finding Status / consequence Response
Training targets are 12 part-grade labels, not four whole-fish grades Confirmed; output cannot establish per-fish localization or counting Preserve the old part model. Add a separate four-grade instance workflow, with an explicit annotation contract. Reject part labels passed off as fish labels.
No parent-fish associations Confirmed; nearest head/body/tail can belong to different fish Generate optional geometry-based annotation DRAFTS for review only. Do not train or count from them automatically.
No independent evaluation images Confirmed; loss/demos cannot demonstrate generalization Require reviewed group-separated train/validation/test data. Do not fabricate val=train.
Confidence .25, IoU .7 and max_det=100 were not tuned Confirmed settings, but no evidence the cap binds: max current GT is 23 parts Replay original settings for the baseline; validation-sweep confidence, NMS, inference head and resolution. Log detection-limit hits.
Detector feature agreement appeared in JSON, while image overlays still showed YOLO labels Confirmed implementation mismatch For a validated feature-regrading variant, both overlays and JSON use the resolved predicted grade. Preserve detector score and separately report uncalibrated feature score.
Body features were fitted on annotated crops and used on predicted crops Confirmed train/inference crop shift Evaluate the second stage on predicted validation boxes, not only ideal GT crops. Keep detector boxes fixed for feature ablations.
Dark-line response is not crack localization Confirmed method limitation Keep it a diagnostic proxy, excluded from the grading feature sets. Do not infer a defect from every edge.
Width/height of axis-aligned boxes is orientation dependent Confirmed geometry limitation Implement PCA-axis width profiles, rotated rectangles, area/length squared, and mask-quality fallback.
RGB/Lab/HSV calculations use an approximate dark-mat mask Confirmed; may drop dark tissue or include neighboring fish Log quality/overlap flags; disable shape regrading on questionable masks; treat thresholds as exploratory. Learned whole-instance masks remain future work.
Export images are already equalized and reduced Confirmed from files/provenance Keep the old pipeline for old-model replay; preserve native new images without an extra enhancement layer. Do not claim equalization can be undone.
Weighted YOLO26 training loss changes as head weights change Confirmed algorithm detail Log the weights and fixed-head component losses; do not compare the aggregate as a constant metric or proof of improved detection.
New data cannot simply resume the same old experiment Confirmed old exact-hash guard and target change Give every run an immutable output folder, fingerprint data/groups/settings, enforce strict same-run resume, and preserve v2 checkpoints.

The new four-grade detector is the most practical first implementation for the requested target: one box enclosing each visible grading instance and one grade for that instance. It is not a whole-image classifier. A two-stage grade-agnostic fish detector plus learned crop classifier remains a worthwhile alternative after this baseline has reliable labels and evaluation. The current implementation adds an optional feature regrader, not a newly trained standalone CNN grade head.

4. B versus C: the body-width hypothesis

A fresh pass measured all 4,995 body regions. The procedure isolates an approximate bright foreground, selects the largest component, estimates its principal longitudinal axis, measures perpendicular widths along 16 slices, and normalizes by robust longitudinal extent. This is visible 2-D body-region shape, NOT physical thickness, calibrated length, or whole-fish shape. Perspective and bending are not eliminated.

Per-photo medians prevent treating all boxes from one frame as separate observations. Photos still share unknown physical specimens and capture sessions, so the effect sizes below are descriptive, not independent-population tests.

Body-shape measurement B median C median Hedges g: C minus B
p90 transverse width / PCA length, all pure-grade photos .538 .612 .67
Same measure after overlap/edge/component checks .566 .599 .34
Rotated-rectangle short/long ratio, screened .677 .661 -.05

The unfiltered comparison uses 80 B and 434 C source photos. The screened comparison uses 75 B and 389 C photos with usable regions. Its underlying mask screen retained 2,317 of 4,995 body regions across all grades. The observed probability that a C measurement exceeds a B measurement drops from about 69.7% to 59.3% for the p90 ratio.

Conclusion: there is a candidate shape association, but it is fragile to measurement choice and region quality. Do not hard-code wider = C. Median-width and area/length-squared also show differences in these images; none establish causality or performance on new fish. The code tests shape against a color+texture comparator trained and applied on the same shape-eligible subset, so any apparent gain is not merely caused by changing which crops are used.

Upper brightness percentiles, highlight candidates and some texture statistics also differ descriptively. Mean yellowness is not a reliable positive C signal here. Lighting, equalization, session, mask and annotation style remain confounded. The feature measurements are suitable for hypothesis generation; improvement requires independent validation. A specular candidate is not an oil-content measurement. A standard planar reference and consistent pose are needed for physical size; they cannot be recovered from pixel width alone.

5. Multi-fish detection: choices and tradeoffs

Chosen first: YOLO26 Small with four reviewed fish-instance grades, 640 input baseline, native-resolution new source files, manual PyTorch training loop, validation-selected checkpoint. Small matches the demonstrated T4 workflow and avoids assuming a larger model repairs wrong supervision.

960 input: included as an inference comparison, not automatically declared superior. A 960-square tensor contains 2.25 times the pixels of 640-square. Runtime and activation memory generally increase; parameter memory does not scale the same way. Upsampling legacy 640x360 photographs cannot restore missing crack detail. Native higher-resolution captures are more useful for detail.

Tiling: optional full-image plus overlapping tiles, enabled for comparison only when validation sources exceed 960 pixels. The full-image pass covers objects cut by tile boundaries; tile-edge exclusions and duplicate merging are implemented. More passes increase latency. Tiling may help small objects but can lose whole-fish context, invent repeated detections, or change apparent color/texture scale. It is not the automatic default for the current low-resolution images.

NMS versus NMS-free head: YOLO26 exposes both heads. The pinned API uses nms=True for one-to-many plus suppression and nms=False for one-to-one. Separate model instances are loaded so inference fusion cannot destroy a branch needed by a later experiment. Both heads and suppression settings are validation experiments. No gain is claimed for either on tamban.

Grade-exclusive suppression: optional, not blanket class-agnostic suppression. Competing grades can describe one object, but two heavily overlapping fish are also real. The code compares this tradeoff instead of always deleting an overlapping lower-score fish. For old part-model diagnostics, heads are never suppressed against bodies merely for overlap.

Instance segmentation: potentially valuable for overlapping silhouettes and shape/color measurements, but it requires reviewed whole-instance masks. The current backups are part masks with unequal annotation styles. This release deliberately implements a box baseline rather than claiming a segmentation model was trained.

Counting: count visible, annotated grading items under a declared policy. A separate detached head cannot be safely matched to its original body from a still image. The output supplies total visible grading-item count and counts per grade; intact-biological-fish count remains unknown unless that target is separately annotated. Do not call twelve part boxes twelve fish.

6. Defects and required additional labels

The existing Rejected labels teach a grade association, not an explanation such as 'a crack is located here.' An explicit defect branch would need reviewed boxes/masks for visible cracks, tears, holes and exposed tissue, plus parent-instance IDs and severity. A minimal crack can remain A; intact fish can be Rejected.

A physically absent head or tail should normally be recorded as an instance attribute, not a box around empty background. Use states such as present, physically missing, occluded, outside frame and uncertain. For visible defects use location masks/boxes. For absence use instance-level supervision and visibility context. This version does not manufacture those labels or infer missing parts from non-detections.

7. Evaluation and controlled comparisons implemented

The baseline must use the same target as the comparison. Old 12-part mAP cannot be compared directly to new whole-fish mAP as if only the architecture changed.

The workbench implements:

  • Class-agnostic IoU matching for localization precision/recall and separating wrong grade from missed fish.
  • Per-grade end-to-end precision/recall/F1 including missed and spurious objects.
  • Matched-only grading metrics, clearly separated from end-to-end scores.
  • 101-point box AP over IoU .50:.95, AP50 and per-grade AP, plus class-agnostic localization AP. This is a documented COCO-style implementation for exhaustive box labels with no ignored/crowd regions, not a claim of identical full official COCO evaluation.
  • Confusion matrix with background/missed/extra categories, CSV and PNG.
  • Count MAE, RMSE, signed bias and per-class count errors; capture-group bootstrap interval for count MAE, with few-group warnings.
  • Crowded-versus-less-crowded reports. The default crowding flag is at least eight GT items or a GT-box pair IoU of .1; it is an annotation-based proxy, not human-labeled occlusion severity.
  • Ranked real failure galleries showing misses, wrong grades, extra predictions and duplicate candidates. Labels must be exhaustive for these diagnoses to be valid.

Each validation experiment uses the same checkpoint and val images. The sweep varies input size, inference head, NMS overlap, grade-exclusive duplicate suppression, optional tiling, and confidence. Feature variants reuse baseline detections, compare color then texture, and compare shape on matched eligibility rules. All scores and timing are retained. Selection uses validation macro end-to-end grade F1, then count MAE. This is an explicit design choice, not a population-optimal objective.

The chosen weights, data fingerprint, preprocessing/inference policy and optional feature model are locked before test. Test requires a separate explicit action and creates a used-test marker; the software refuses routine reuse of the same locked test. Human discipline is still required: software cannot prove an external test set was never viewed or a specimen ID is correct.

For training experiments such as model size, rotation augmentation or sampling, run separate new experiments with identical data groups and other settings. Compare multiple random seeds when feasible. Repeated tuning on a small validation set can itself overfit; the untouched test and sufficiently diverse groups matter more than a large sweep.

8. Priorities and readiness

Critical: establish reviewed whole-fish boxes and a fragment-counting convention; acquire or confirm independent physical-specimen and batch metadata; create all-grade validation/test groups; inspect the real checkpoint and predictions before diagnosing learned-model failures. Do not pretend a renamed 12-class dataset meets a four-class instance target.

Important: collect B and C together under shared capture settings, prioritize independent A/B specimens, retain native unenhanced originals, verify masks and borderline vendor labels, test resolution/thresholds on validation, document confidence as uncalibrated.

Optional: segmentation, a learned second-stage crop network, validated defect localization, calibrated confidence, class-image sampling, rotation augmentation and larger models. They should be retained only when controlled results justify their cost.

Status now: original part baseline trained according to the user's logs; code/data audit and revised implementation completed; 36 automated tests passed; synthetic reviewed-data importer and CPU loader checked; new feature extraction/save-reload smoke-tested on 20 actual regions. Real YOLO retraining, inference-head comparisons, feature gains, independent metrics, and final-test results are not yet verified.
